nodes.name: Lemma 2.27: Partite
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a relational language, $\mathcal U$ be a closure description in $L$,
$\mathbf {A}$ be a finite $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure and $\mathbf {B}$ be a finite $\mathcal U$-semi-closed $\mathbf {A}$-partite $L$-system such that every vertex of $\mathbf {B}$ is contained in a copy of $\mathbf {A}$.
Then there exists a finite $\mathcal U$-semi-closed $\mathbf {A}$-partite $L$-system $\mathbf {C}$
such that 
$$
\mathbf {C}\longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.
$$
(Here we consider $\mathbf {A}$ to be an $\mathbf {A}$-partite system and thus all copies of $\mathbf {A}$ in $\mathbf {B}$ preserve parts.)

Moreover there exists a family $\mathcal B$ of copies of $\mathbf {B}$ in $\mathbf {C}$ such that:
\begin{enumerate} 
\item For every $2$-colouring of all substructures of $\mathbf {C}$ which are isomorphic to $\mathbf {A}$ there exists $\widetilde{\mathbf {B}}\in \mathcal B$ such that all substructures of $\widetilde{\mathbf {B}}$ which are isomorphic to $\mathbf {A}$ are monochromatic (thus $\mathcal B$ is a Ramsey system of copies of $\mathbf {B}$ in $\mathbf {C}$).
\item Every $\widetilde{\mathbf {B}}\in \mathcal B$ is a $\mathcal U$-substructure of $\mathbf {C}$.
\end{enumerate}
Finally, if $\mathbf {B}$ is $\mathcal U$-closed then $\mathbf {C}$ is $\mathcal U$-closed, too, and if every $\mathcal U$-irreducible substructure of $\mathbf {B}$ is transversal, then every $\mathcal U$-irreducible substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ is transversal, too.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.21: Ramsey Property of ordered structures
nodes.statement:
Let $L$  be a relational language containing a binary relation $\leq$
and $\mathcal E$ be a (possibly infinite) family of ordered irreducible $L$-struc\-tures.
Then the class of all finite ordered structures in $\mathop{\mathrm{Age}}\nolimits(\mathop{\mathrm{Forb_e}}\nolimits(\mathcal E))$ is a Ramsey class.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.29: Partite construction for $\mathcal U$ -substructures
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a relational language,
let $\mathcal U$ be a closure description in $L$, let $\mathbf {A}$ and $\mathbf {B}$ be finite $\mathcal U$-closed
$L$-structures and let $\mathbf {C}_0$ be a finite $L$-structure such that
$$
\mathbf {C}_0 \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.
$$
Further assume that every copy of $\mathbf {A}$ in $\mathbf {C}_0$ is in fact a $\mathcal U$-substructure of $\mathbf {C}_0$.
Then there exists a finite $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure $\mathbf {C}$ with a $\mathcal U$-homomorphism-embedding $\mathbf {C}\to \mathbf {C}_0$ such that:
$$
\mathbf {C} \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2
$$
and every $\mathcal U$-irreducible substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ isomorphic to a substructure of $\mathbf {B}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.28: $\mathcal U$ -closed partite construction
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a relational language,
let $\mathcal U$ be a closure description in $L$, let $\mathbf {A}$ and $\mathbf {B}$ be finite $\mathcal U$-closed
$L$-structures and let $\mathbf {C}_0$ be a finite $L$-structure such that
$$
\mathbf {C}_0 \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.
$$
Then there exists a finite $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure $\mathbf {C}$ with a $\mathcal U$-homomorphism-embed{\-}ding $\mathbf {C}\to \mathbf {C}_0$ such that:
$$
\mathbf {C} \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2
$$
and every $\mathcal U$-irreducible substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ is isomorphic to a substructure of $\mathbf {B}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.30, Lemma 2.31: Iterated partite construction
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a relational language, let $\mathcal U$ be a closure description in $L$, let $\mathcal K$ be a strong amalgamation class of finite irreducible $\mathcal U$-closed
$L$-structures which is hereditary for $\mathcal U$-closed substructures and let $j\geq 0$ be a non-negative integer.
Let $\mathbf {A},\mathbf {B}\in \mathcal K$
and let $\mathbf {C}_0$ be a finite $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure such that $$\mathbf {C}_0 \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.$$
Further assume that either $j=0$ or $j>0$ and every $\mathcal U$-closed substructure of $\mathbf {C}_0$ with $\mathcal U$-size at most $j$ has a $({\mathcal K},\mathcal U)$-completion. 
Then there exists a $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure $\mathbf {C}$ satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=0em]
\item There is a $\mathcal U$-homo{\-}morphism-embedding $\mathbf {C}\to \mathbf {C}_0$,
\item $\mathbf {C} \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2$,
\item every $\mathcal U$-closed substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ of $\mathcal U$-size at most $j+1$ has a $({\mathcal K},\mathcal U)$-completion, and
\item every $\mathcal U$-irreducible substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ is isomorphic to a substructure of $\mathbf {B}$. 
\end{enumerate}

Let $L$ be a relational language, let $\mathcal U$ be a closure description in $L$, let $\mathcal K$ be a strong amalgamation class of finite irreducible $\mathcal U$-closed
$L$-structures which is hereditary for $\mathcal U$-closed substructures.
Let $\mathbf {A},\mathbf {B}\in \mathcal K$, let $n\geq 1$ be an integer,
and let $\mathbf {C}_0$ be a finite $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure such that $$\mathbf {C}_0 \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.$$

Then there exists a finite $\mathcal U$-closed $L$-structure $\mathbf {C}$ with a $\mathcal U$-homomorphism-embedding $\mathbf {C}\to \mathbf {C}_0$
such that
$$\mathbf {C} \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.$$
Moreover, every $\mathcal U$-substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ with at most $n$ vertices has a $({\mathcal K},\mathcal U)$-completion
and every $\mathcal U$-irreducible substructure of $\mathbf {C}$ is isomorphic to a substructure of $\mathbf {B}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.11: Ramsey property of locally finite strong amalgamation classes
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a language, let $\mathcal R$ be a Ramsey class of irreducible finite $L$-structures and let ${\mathcal K}$ be a hereditary
locally finite subclass of $\mathcal R$ with the strong amalgamation property.
Then ${\mathcal K}$ is a Ramsey class.

Explicitly:
For every pair of struc\-tures $\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B}\in{\mathcal K}$ there exists
a structure $\mathbf {C} \in {\mathcal K}$  such that
$$
\mathbf {C} \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.
$$

nodes.name: Theorem 2.18: Ramsey property of multiamalgamation classes
nodes.statement: Every $(\mathcal R,\mathcal U)$-multiamalgamation class ${\mathcal K}$ is Ramsey.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.19: $\vv{\mathop{\mathrm{Str}}\nolimits}(L)$ is Ramsey
nodes.statement: For every language $L$ (possibly involving both relations and functions) containing a binary relation $\leq$ the class $\vv{\mathop{\mathrm{Str}}\nolimits}(L)$ is a Ramsey class.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.17: Explicit description of lift of $\mathop{\mathrm{Forb_{he}}}\nolimits({\mathcal F})$
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a family of finite connected $L$-structures which is
closed for homomorphism-embedding images.  Denote by ${\cal L}_\mathcal F$ the
class of all finite maximal ${\mathcal F}$-lifts.  Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Age}}\nolimits({\cal L}_\mathcal F)$ is an amalgamation class
with strong amalgamations whose shadows are free amalgamations.
If ${\mathcal F}$ is a regular family, then the ${\mathcal F}$-lift adds only finitely many new relations
of every arity and therefore is precompact.

If ${\cal L}_\mathcal F$ is countable, denote by $\mathbf {U}'$ the Fra\"{\i}ss\' e{} limit of $\mathop{\mathrm{Age}}\nolimits({\cal L}_\mathcal F)$.
If ${\mathcal F}$ is regular and $L$ is a finite relational language, then the shadow
$\mathbf {U}=\mathop{\mathrm{Sh}}\nolimits(\mathbf {U}')\in\mathop{\mathrm{Forb_{he}}}\nolimits({\mathcal F})$ is the $\omega$-categorical existentially complete
structure universal for $\mathop{\mathrm{Forb_{he}}}\nolimits({\mathcal F})$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.23: Ramsey property of lifts of classes…
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a language containing a binary relation  $\leq$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a (possibly infinite) regular family of finite connected weakly ordered $L$-structures which is closed for homomorphism-embedding images.
Further assume that the class of all finite ordered structures in $\mathop{\mathrm{Forb_{he}}}\nolimits(\mathcal F)$ is a locally finite subclass of the class of all finite ordered $L$-structures.
Then the class $\mathcal K$ of all finite ordered structures in $\mathop{\mathrm{Forb_{he}}}\nolimits({\mathcal F})$ has a precompact Ramsey lift.

More specifically:
The class $\mathcal K_{\mathcal F}$ of all ordered maximal ${\mathcal F}$-lifts of structures in $\mathcal K$ is a Ramsey class
and
for every pair of struc\-tures $\mathbf {A}, \mathbf {B}\in\mathcal K_\mathcal F$ there exists a 
structure $\mathbf {C} \in \mathcal K_\mathcal F$  such that
$$
\mathbf {C} \longrightarrow (\mathbf {B})^{\mathbf {A}}_2.
$$
If $L$ is a relational language then the lift $\mathcal K_\mathcal F$ has the lift property
with respect to ${\mathcal K}$.
